abstract: A modification of Tulsi’s quantum search algorithm with intermediate measurements of the control is presented. In order to analyze the effect of measurements in quantum searches, a different choice of the angular parameter is used. The study is performed for several values of time lapses between measurements, finding close relationships between probabilities and correlations (Mutual Information and Cumulative Correlation Measure). The order of this modified algorithm is estimated, showing that for some time lapses the performance is improved, and became of order $O(N)$ (classical brute force search) when the measurement is taken in every step. The results indicate a possible way to analyze improvements to other quantum algorithms using one, or more, control qubits.

specification.problem: Reconstruct a modified Tulsi quantum search algorithm in which the control qubit is measured intermediately, with a different choice of angular parameter. Study how the time lapse between measurements affects success probability, correlations (Mutual Information, Cumulative Correlation Measure) and the algorithm's order, which becomes O(N) when measuring at every step.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Small finite-instance reconstruction of the search with a control qubit and intermediate control measurements. The abstract does not give the exact oracle, angle definition or circuit, so only the generic structure and background search relations are specified. Eq_2 is a Grover-type stand-in, not the paper's formula.

symbols.meaning: Number of algorithm steps between control measurements (time lapse)
Angular parameter of the search rotation
Probability of finding the marked item after t steps

equations.label: Brute-force order
equations.description: The order of the modified algorithm becomes classical brute-force search when the control is measured at every step.
equations.abstract_quote: became of order $O(N)$ (classical brute force search) when the measurement is taken in every step

equations.label: Rotation-angle success probability
equations.description: Standard Grover-type amplitude amplification with a single marked item, valid only for coherent evolution between measurements. Tulsi's version uses a different angular parameter, not specified here. Intermediate measurements break this coherent form.
equations.justification: Textbook background for amplitude-amplification-type search, not claimed to be the paper's exact formula.
assumptions: Unmeasured coherent evolution between control measurements

registers.name: search
registers.role: Holds the database index; marked item searched

registers.name: control
registers.role: Control qubit of the Tulsi-type search, measured intermittently every tau steps

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over the search register tensored with a control qubit in an assumed fixed state (e.g. |0> or |+>; not given in the abstract)

steps.description: Prepare the search register in uniform superposition and initialize the control qubit.
Apply one Tulsi-type search iteration (controlled oracle and diffusion-like operators with the chosen angle theta), rotating amplitude toward the marked item.
Repeat the iteration for tau steps coherently, then measure the control qubit; repeat this block until the total step count is reached.
For tau = 1 (measurement at every step) the performance degrades to classical-like scaling.

specification.measurement: Intermediate projective measurement of the control qubit every tau steps (basis assumed computational); final measurement of the search register in the computational basis to read out the marked item.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate success probability P_t versus tau from repeated runs or simulation; compute Mutual Information and Cumulative Correlation Measure from the resulting state or distributions; fit scaling of steps needed versus N to estimate the order.
assumptions: Standard Grover-type rotation used as background for the unspecified Tulsi dynamics
Control measured in computational basis, with outcomes either averaged or post-selected (unspecified)
missing_information: Exact Tulsi oracle and control-qubit circuit
Definition of the chosen angular parameter
Measurement basis and post-measurement handling of the control
Definitions of Mutual Information and Cumulative Correlation Measure as used
Whether control outcomes are averaged or post-selected
